name: Campaigns
title: Campaigns: operator and guest paths and what can go wrong

BANDS.s: Marketing email address, Twilio marketing number, monthly text limit and who may approve in MoM
Choose a creation mode, act on a suggestion or open a campaign to see its available actions.
The dedicated email and SMS builders have four steps. The multichannel builder has six.
Check eligibility and credit reservations, then follow the chosen launch or owner review path.
Follow queued or scheduled work into dispatch, channel outcomes and status changes.
What the guest gets by email or text and what they do with it
Edit a returned campaign, duplicate it, inspect its history or follow it to completion.
Compare delivery, engagement, returning guests, attributed orders and sales.
Check which actions the current status permits and how results count returning guests.

NODES.d: A restaurant operator or AIO staff member can create a custom promotion or base it on a deal, spotlight, menu item or special day and choose the channels that will carry it.
e: Operator does not know that email and text need a sender address and a registered number first
Location chosen in the restaurant switcher is not the one the operator means to market for
Campaign built for the wrong location

NODES.d: At send time a verified, enabled restaurant domain can provide the From address. The feature and sending switches must allow it. The AIO address covers an ineligible domain, a failed lookup or a rejected custom sender.
e: A restaurant expects a branded sender while verification is pending
The sender changes between preview and the scheduled send
The restaurant cannot explain the address on the received email
The selected sender or reply address belongs to another restaurant
Guest replies reach the wrong restaurant

NODES.d: A business needs a marketing number with an accepted verification status to submit a campaign with SMS. Delivery also needs the configured sender and Twilio subaccount. Check a configuration change again at send time.
e: Number not yet approved for A2P 10DLC or toll-free verification but marked verified in AIO
Texts filtered by carriers, sent count looks fine
Twilio configuration removed or changed after approval, relay skips the text pages without marking them failed
Campaign shows sent zero with no reason
Verification changes after the operator selects SMS
A previously available campaign channel cannot launch
Sub-account auth token rotated in Twilio but not in AIO

NODES.d: The monthly marketing text allowance is shared with Journeys. A campaign reserves credits for eligible SMS guests, one per SMS or two per MMS recipient. Cancelling a scheduled send or rejecting a campaign releases its reservation.
e: Reservation counts against the month of submission, not the month the campaign is scheduled to send
Next month's send blocks this month's quota
Month boundary taken from server time, not the restaurant time zone
Late evening submissions land in the wrong month
Reserved texts for guests with invalid numbers or later opt outs are never released
Limit used up by texts that were never sent
Threshold alert goes nowhere when the location has no Marketing email
Restaurant hits the limit with no warning
Limit is per location while the Twilio account and bill are per business

NODES.d: Only MoM users whose role grants the campaign approve permission for that location can approve, request edits or reject. A reminder job pushes a Review campaign notification to their online devices while campaigns wait in Sent for Review.
e: No user at the location holds the approve permission
Approver has MoM installed but no online device registered, so the reminder never arrives
Staff member who left still holds the approve permission
Wrong person approves sends to the guest list

NODES.d: An empty restaurant sees the welcome view. The dashboard has campaign results, suggestions and a searchable list. Combine status, channel and type filters. Clearing filters preserves the search text.
e: A previous restaurant or filter still limits the list
Clearing filters leaves a search term unnoticed

NODES.t: Choose an entry or a row action
NODES.d: Start an email, SMS or multichannel campaign, or use a contextual suggestion. The row and detail panel offer actions based on the stored status and selected channels.
e: A status changes while the action menu is open
An action fails and the operator needs to reload
The operator starts multichannel when only one channel was intended
Extra steps or unintended placements are included

NODES.d: Custom is the default. The other choices use a deal, spotlight, menu item or special day. Custom uses the operator description. Legacy Events is hidden.
e: Changing the campaign type clears a previously chosen offer
The operator launches with the wrong content
Deal later edited or deactivated in Deals while the campaign still promotes it
Guests sent an offer that no longer works
Menu item later deleted or hidden in Menu Manager
Campaign links to an item guests cannot order
Deal list offers expired or future deals
Campaign promotes an offer that is not live
Custom special day created with a past date
Campaign about a day already gone

NODES.d: Enter the campaign title and check name availability. For Custom, add the description used to prepare content. Record-backed types supply their own context.
e: Two operators pick the same name at the same moment, both pass the check
Custom campaign copy is built from an outdated description
The draft advertises the wrong offer

NODES.d: The multichannel flow asks for channels. The dedicated email and SMS flows preset the channel and open content directly after campaign type. Kiosk and Mega kiosk can include a banner, screensaver or both.
e: Text chosen for a location without a verified marketing number, no warning until final submit
Removing a channel on edit leaves its old content and results attached
Operator assumes Email reaches all guests, but only subscribed guests with valid emails count

NODES.d: Choose an audience using the available guest filters and inspect eligible recipients for each message channel. A message channel with no eligible audience needs attention before launch. SMS also checks verification and remaining credits.
e: A delayed eligibility estimate belongs to the previous filter selection
The operator misjudges audience size and SMS cost
Allergen filter includes guests with the allergen when the offer is meant to avoid them
Segment or spend tier recalculated between approval and send, list is not refreshed
Guests who left the segment still receive it
Guests shared across locations of the same business filtered per location only
Multi-location guest gets the same campaign from each location
Filters combine as all must match, operator expects any

NODES.d: The email builder fills heading, text, image and call to action from the deal, spotlight or item, styled from the Brand Book. Custom HTML sections are sanitised on save. The finished email is uploaded as an HTML file, up to 30 MB, and must keep the unsubscribe placeholder.
e: Media card colours lack brand swatches, the header uses a fixed colour, or text lacks heading and body styles
The operator must restyle each email by hand
Custom HTML removes the unsubscribe placeholder, email goes out with no working unsubscribe link
Sanitiser strips styles or links the operator pasted
Email looks different from the preview
Brand Book colours or fonts changed after the email was built, saved HTML keeps the old style
Image file names with spaces or very large images break or slow the email
Call to action points at a test or temporary online ordering link
Guests land on a dead page
HTML upload fails mid-wizard and the error is not shown
Operator submits an email with no template

NODES.d: The operator can ask the AI assistant service to generate or regenerate campaign copy and images for the chosen type. The call times out after 30 seconds.
e: AI states a discount, price or date that differs from the actual deal
Guests promised an offer the restaurant does not honour
Generation takes over 30 seconds and fails with a generic error
Regenerate overwrites edits the operator made by hand
AI copy includes claims such as health or allergen statements

NODES.d: The composer allows 130 characters for SMS. An image switches it to MMS, with up to 1,500 characters and a displayed cost of two texts. It validates links and excludes emojis. Inspect the final content and opt-out line.
e: Opt-out line appended again each time the form is submitted, so an edited campaign shows it twice
Opt-out line added only by Web Dash, a campaign saved another way has none
An image changes the displayed cost from one text to two after audience selection
Projected usage and available credits disagree
Restaurant name missing from the message body
MMS image too large or wrong type for carriers
Text delivered without the image or fails

NODES.t: Preview and send a test email
NODES.d: Email and SMS quick creation show an inline preview while content is written. Multichannel creation has a separate preview step. Email also supports a test send.
e: Test email subject is not the real subject
No test text message, the first real text is the first time anyone sees it
Broken links or formatting reach every guest
Test endpoint sends any HTML to any address without a limit
Abuse of the restaurant sender address
Test reports success when queued even if delivery later fails
Preview frame differs from real mail clients, for example dark mode or Outlook

NODES.t: Choose send time and end date
NODES.d: Choose immediate or scheduled launch. A placement shown for a period needs an end date. Email or SMS alone has no placement end date. A linked deal limits its campaign schedule.
e: Schedule taken in the operator browser time zone, not the restaurant's
Send at the wrong local hour
Send at a scheduled time before approval arrives, campaign expires instead of sending late
Texts allowed at any hour, including night time
A screen end date is earlier than the operator intended
Guests stop seeing the placement before the promotion finishes
Deal end changed later, campaign end is not moved with it

NODES.d: Save progress as a draft, send for owner review, or choose direct launch and confirm. Launch follows the selected schedule.
e: Wizard data in browser storage restored into a different campaign or location
Double click on submit creates two campaigns
Guests receive the same campaign twice

NODES.d: Select the social destinations, prepare their copy and media, and inspect the preview for each chosen platform. Connection and media requirements can differ by destination.
e: A disconnected account stays selected in the final preview
A crop or caption fits one platform but cuts off a condition on another

NODES.d: Configure the selected placement content and review the corresponding website, online, QR, kiosk or menu board preview. Check the destination size and location.
e: Kiosk banner art is reused at full screen and crops the offer price
A QR placement opens an incorrect restaurant destination

NODES.d: A Draft is stored with its content, tags and allergens but no audience snapshot, no text reservation and no end of campaign event.
e: Draft saved with a schedule date that passes before it is resumed
Submitting later fails or expires at once
Referenced deal or item deleted while the campaign is a draft

NODES.d: Submission validates the content and resolves eligible contacts for the selected restaurant and channels. A guest can qualify for one channel while lacking consent or a deliverable address for the other.
e: Snapshot taken at submit, guest who unsubscribes or opts out before a later send still receives it
Failure after the campaign row is saved removes only the campaign, content rows are left behind
Guests with non-US phone numbers silently excluded
Guests imported with consent assumed rather than recorded
Large guest lists resolved in one query at submit
Submit times out for big tenants

NODES.d: Check the eligible SMS count against monthly credits and reserve the required balance on submission. An over-limit submission must be revised. A returned edit follows the review choice recorded by the owner. Email-only campaigns proceed without an SMS reservation.
e: Limit exceeded message does not say how many texts remain or when it resets
Journeys use the same pool, an automated journey takes the room a planned campaign needed
A returned edit launches under the recorded review setting before the operator expects
The owner misses the intended final check

NODES.d: The campaign is saved as Sent for Review. A reminder job looks for campaigns in review and pushes a Review campaign notification to approvers' online MoM devices, opening the To Review tab.
e: Reminder repeats for every pending campaign on every run
Push fails for one device and stops the rest for that tenant
Operator in Web Dash gets no notice when the owner acts
Campaign sits unnoticed in Needs Edits

NODES.d: An authorised owner can approve, request edits with a reason, or reject. When returning work, the owner can require another review or allow launch after the edits. Check the current status and the schedule before acting.
e: MoM preview differs from the email and text the guest will get
Two approvers act at once, both pass the status check
The owner requests edits without selecting the intended review preference
The revised campaign follows the wrong approval path
Status change uses the location from the approver's session, approver with access to several locations acts on the wrong one

NODES.t: Approve, return for edits or reject
NODES.d: Approval starts immediate launch or schedules delivery. A returned edit follows the owner’s re-review choice. Rejection releases the SMS reservation. A missed review window can expire.
e: Needs Edits releases nothing, the text reservation stays held while the campaign waits
Rejection reason not shown in Web Dash
Operator does not know what to fix
The operator misreads whether a returned edit needs another review
A corrected campaign launches before the owner expects

NODES.d: Prepare pages of eligible email and SMS recipients for the selected channels. Provider acceptance, delivery, suppression and failure can occur at different times.
e: One page query fails, those 50 guests are skipped with only a log line
Part of the audience never receives it
Guest list for a scheduled send is fixed at approval, days before the send
Re-triggering publish on a re-approval queues every page again
Guest email and phone travel inside queue messages
Personal data spread in queue logs

NODES.d: Right away pages go to the campaign queue at once. Scheduled pages become timed events, one per channel and page, named by environment, tenant, location, campaign, action and page.
e: Queueing errors only logged, approval shows success even when nothing was queued
Edit after approval does not remove the old scheduled pages
Old and new versions both send

NODES.d: Pages go to a first in first out queue grouped by the Twilio sub-account for text, or by tenant and location, so one restaurant's pages are sent in order.
e: Large campaigns from one business block its other texts in the same group
Order ready texts or journeys delayed
Message redelivered after a timeout and processed twice

NODES.d: The send date, time and offset are taken from the stored schedule and registered with the scheduler, which fires the page events at that moment.
e: Offset taken from the server, not the restaurant, so the send fires hours off
Send at the wrong local time
Daylight saving change between scheduling and sending shifts the send by an hour
Send at the wrong local time
Scheduler event creation fails and only a log records it

NODES.t: Check that the send is still current
NODES.d: The relay checks campaign status, the saved schedule and end events before dispatch. A cancelled or superseded timed event must leave the current draft or rescheduled campaign alone.
e: An old scheduled event survives a cancellation or reschedule
Guests receive a campaign outside the chosen window
A status changes while pages are being processed
The operator sees incomplete or delayed totals

NODES.d: The email relay fetches the template, resolves the sender, adds guest tracking and unsubscribe information, and records the provider outcome for each recipient.
e: The same campaign email is delivered repeatedly after approval
Template file missing or unreachable, every email in the page fails
Failed sends are counted but never retried
Sending faster than the email service rate limit causes throttling errors
Unsubscribe placeholder missing, link never inserted
No List-Unsubscribe header for one-click unsubscribe
Gmail and Yahoo bulk sender rules breached, spam placement

NODES.d: The relay sends the prepared text and optional media through the configured Twilio account. It suppresses repeated sends to the same number for that campaign content for up to 24 hours, and records provider outcomes.
e: A late retry arrives after the 24 hour SMS duplicate protection expires
A guest may receive the same text twice
Number opted out at Twilio fails with an error but AIO consent is not updated
Repeated failed attempts and wrong reach
Whole page sent in parallel, carrier throughput limits exceeded
Failed texts still counted against the monthly limit

NODES.d: The email service reports deliveries, bounces and complaints through its events configuration, and Twilio reports message status and link clicks. These are written against the send logs.
e: Hard bounces and spam complaints not turned into unsubscribes
Sender reputation falls, later campaigns land in spam
Delivery events not reflected in campaign results, which only show accepted or failed at send
Events configuration name missing in an environment

NODES.d: The relay attempts a post for each selected social account and records success or failure separately. Inspect each destination after a partial failure.
e: One provider rejects the post while another succeeds
Only part of the intended audience sees the offer
Retry reposts to an account that already succeeded
Duplicate promotion appears in the feed

NODES.d: Eligible active campaigns supply featured placements. Ending a campaign changes its status. Check when each guest screen stops showing the placement. The underlying deal retains its own availability rules.
e: Expired campaign stays in a menu board playlist after a status change
A selected website placement has no published campaign for the restaurant

NODES.d: Compare a configured placement with the physical screen at that location. On Android POS, the idle customer display loads media from its device settings. A campaign marked Active in Web Dash does not establish that the media was sent to that display.
e: Only one kiosk orientation displays the configured content
The register loads a new image or video but the idle display has no button label
The customer sees the fallback screen instead of the promotion
The replacement image fails to download and the display still has the previous image saved
Guests may continue to see an earlier offer

NODES.d: The guest receives the email with the selected sender, campaign content, call to action and personal unsubscribe link.
e: Email lands in spam or promotions
Images blocked or broken in the mail client
Guest receives the same campaign from two locations of the same business
Email not readable with a screen reader, images without alternative text

NODES.d: An open event can be recorded for a delivered email. The reported open rate filters recognised privacy prefetches and likely bots. Image blocking and unmeasured historical sends can still affect interpretation.
e: An automatic image load is misclassified as a human open
Images blocked so real opens are not counted

NODES.d: The call to action or text link opens the restaurant website or online ordering. Online ordering and QR show published, live campaigns that match the guest's segment, spend, tags and allergens, excluding Deals type campaigns.
e: Deal promoted in the email is not applied automatically on online ordering
Guest pays full price and complains
Link opens the wrong location of a multi-location restaurant
Guest orders from the wrong store
Email clicks are not tracked, only Twilio link clicks for texts
Deal reached its usage limit or ended before the guest acts

NODES.d: The unsubscribe link opens a page that posts the guest token; the guest is marked not subscribed and leaves future email audiences.
e: Unsubscribe does not reach pages already queued from the approval snapshot
Unsubscribe token never expires and is guessable from the link pattern
Unsubscribe applies per tenant but guest expects per restaurant, or the reverse

NODES.d: The guest gets the text from the restaurant marketing number, with the link and opt-out line, and an image if one was added.
e: Text arrives late at night in the guest time zone
Guest never gave marketing consent but was imported as opted in

NODES.t: Record a guest SMS opt out or restart
NODES.d: On an inbound event, Twilio supplies its opt-out decision or AIO reads recognised reply text. STOP records opted out. START or UNSTOP records opted in. The handler matches the business, guest phone and restaurant before updating consent.
e: STOP is recorded at Twilio but not in AIO consent
Opt out recorded after the approval snapshot, pages already queued still send
An ordinary reply is mistaken for a change of consent
The guest marketing preference changes unexpectedly
The latest send and guest relationship point to different restaurants
The wrong location retains the previous preference

NODES.d: The guest places an order after seeing a promotion. For sales attribution the order must belong to the same guest and restaurant as a qualifying email or text. Seeing a screen promotion alone does not establish that link.
e: Order cannot be linked to the guest because they check out as a different guest record
Promoted item out of stock at the POS

NODES.d: The guest sees a promotion at a participating website, online or QR placement. Online audience and eligibility restrictions can differ from website featured content.
e: Published campaign is visible on the website but excluded by the online guest filter
Destination does not show the promoted content
Guest follows a placement after the underlying offer retires

NODES.t: Edit a draft or returned campaign
NODES.d: Draft and Needs edits campaigns can be edited. A returned campaign can require review again or proceed to its selected schedule after changes. A Scheduled campaign can be returned to Draft by cancelling its send.
e: The displayed schedule still shows a previously saved end date after an edit
The placement ends at an unexpected time
Content rows rewritten as delete and insert, a failure in between leaves the campaign without content
A user duplicates a scheduled campaign without cancelling its original send
Two independent campaigns may reach the same audience

NODES.d: Duplicate immediately creates a separately named draft with copied channel content and kiosk mappings. The source retains its state. Delivery results and status history belong to their own campaign.
e: Copy keeps the old schedule and end date, which are in the past
Copy keeps a deal or item that no longer exists
Copied email keeps the original template file reference
Edits to the copy change the original

NODES.d: Open the campaign details and inspect the recorded transitions, including when the campaign was sent for review, returned, launched or cancelled.
e: A late status entry appears out of order
The operator cannot reconstruct when the campaign launched
The operator reads the history of a copy instead of its source

NODES.t: Finish a send or reach placement end
NODES.d: An email or SMS only campaign moves from Active to Sent when every selected message channel accounts for its recipients through sends, failures or skips. A campaign with a timed placement can stay Active until that placement ends.
e: End event lost, status only corrected by the nightly job
Campaign shows as running a day late
Expired campaign keeps its text reservation if no event reaches it
Nightly job runs on server time, not restaurant time
End at the wrong local time

NODES.d: Rejection records the reason and releases SMS credits. The operator may duplicate or delete the rejected campaign.
e: Rejected campaign cannot be fixed and resubmitted

NODES.d: Sent records a completed send or ended placement. Expired records a missed campaign window. The detail panel and history explain which outcome occurred.
e: Sent is mistaken for delivery to every guest
The operator overlooks failed or suppressed messages

NODES.d: Inspect the delivery and engagement measures supported by each channel. Email reports delivered messages and human opens. Text reports delivery and tracked link clicks. Read tracking availability alongside failures and suppressions.
e: Sent and failed counts wrong when pages finish at the same time
Historical sends without tracking look like zero opens or clicks
The operator compares measured and unmeasured sends
No export of recipients or results
Cannot reconcile with the email or Twilio bill
Total counts guests at approval, not those actually sent to

NODES.d: Review orders, sales and distinct returning guests after qualifying delivery. One order can appear on multiple campaign detail pages. The restaurant total counts that order and guest once.
e: A guest checks out under another customer record
A qualifying visit cannot be associated with the delivered message
The operator adds the sales on overlapping campaign detail pages
Combined sales exceed the distinct restaurant total

NODES.d: The operator has read the outcome and decides whether to copy or adjust for the next campaign.
e: No guidance on what a good result looks like
Operator cannot improve the next campaign

NODES.d: Confirm direct launch, then send now or at the scheduled time. This path skips the owner review queue.
e: Staff launch a campaign the owner never saw
Old and new status names shown side by side during rollout

NODES.d: Cancel send is available for Scheduled campaigns. Confirmation returns the record to Draft, clears its schedule and releases any SMS reservation. Dispatch checks for stale scheduled events.
e: Cancel does not remove the scheduler events already created
Cancel does not release the text reservation

NODES.d: Delete is available for Draft, Needs edits, Rejected and Expired campaigns. Confirm before removal.
e: Delete removes records that results or send logs still point at
Deletion is confirmed for a similarly named draft
The intended campaign stays in the list and the wrong draft is lost

NODES.d: For each qualifying campaign, the ticket must be created within 30 days of the first qualifying delivery to that guest. Fully paid, partially paid and partially refunded tickets can qualify. Sales use the ticket price after discounts and before tax and tips. Restaurant totals count each ticket and guest once.
e: The operator compares all cash collected at the register with attributed sales before tax and tips
Sales totals differ even when the same tickets are present
A ticket is opened before delivery or before the window closes, then paid on the other side of that boundary
Using payment time to reconcile the report produces a different order list
A guest receives a partial refund and the operator expects the ticket to disappear from the campaign
The qualifying ticket can still contribute its discounted price. The figure can differ from net receipts

NODES.d: An Active campaign with website, online, QR, POS, kiosk or menu board placement can be ended. Confirmation moves it to Sent. An associated deal continues according to its own dates and status.
e: Campaign moves to Sent while a screen keeps showing the offer
Staff end the campaign and assume its linked deal has also ended
The deal can still be available to guests under its own schedule

NODES.d: The dashboard requests due holiday, deal, segment or inactivity suggestions for the current restaurant. The action opens multichannel creation with the suggested details and takes the operator to channel or audience selection.
e: A recommended deal expires between opening the dashboard and preparing the send
A suggested segment changes before launch
Fewer eligible guests qualify than the operator expected

EDGES: Limit exceeded or text not verified

NOTES: Who builds: the live wizard is in Web Dash; the PRD calls the builder the AIO buddy, so AIO staff often build on behalf of the restaurant. Who approves: MoM users whose role grants the campaign approve permission for that location.
Email is sent through the AWS email service (SES) with an events configuration set; the brief's SendGrid label does not apply to campaigns. Mapped as Email service.
PROD 4651 documents duplicate email following approval. Concurrent approvals and email retries are test scenarios. The incident root cause was not provided.

MoM preview rendering, carrier receipt, and whether email bounce or complaint events change the subscription record require separate checks. The internal Twilio worker handles inbound consent changes.
Unsubscribe page host not confirmed; the backend exposes a public unsubscribe endpoint that takes the token.

Android POS reads idle customer display media from device settings and caches downloads. The connection between a Web Dash campaign and that device setting, kiosk rendering and screen refresh timing require separate verification.
The reminder job schedule (how often approvers are pushed) and the nightly end job time were not confirmed.

Quick email and SMS creation use inline preview. Multichannel uses a separate preview step. Direct launch, cancel, end, deletion, status history and attribution are implemented on internal. Production rollout was not established.
